content: Funding has been allocated to enhance school health services, including the provision of nutritious meals and healthy food options. Schools have established systems to plan, monitor, and evaluate the progress and performance of their health services, ensuring quality assurance and adherence to established standards. Efforts are being made to transform every school into a health-promoting institution. This involves developing and implementing a comprehensive curriculum supported by appropriate resources. The implementation of this curriculum is monitored at various levels, including global, national, subnational, local, and school levels. A national education policy or strategy recognizes health-promoting schools (HPS) as a means to achieve national development goals through education, providing a framework for their promotion across the country. Collaboration between local governments, communities, and schools is formalized to support HPS initiatives. Leadership for HPS is distributed among school principals, teachers, administrative staff, school board members, health personnel, students, parents, and caregivers. Regular planning and monitoring systems are in place to oversee the governance and leadership of HPS. Students, parents, caregivers, and families are actively engaged in all aspects of school operations related to HPS. Schools also establish formal and informal partnerships with local community stakeholders, including local governments, to support health-promoting initiatives. School staff are trained to understand the physical, social, and psychological development of students and how these factors influence learning and behavior. The school curriculum integrates physical, social-emotional, and psychological aspects of student health, safety, nutrition, and well-being. Pedagogical approaches and relationships between students and teachers promote health, positive relationships, safety, physical activity, and healthy lifestyles. Staff receive training in health literacy and teaching strategies to support the HPS approach. Comprehensive school health services, including nutrition and food provision, are integrated into school policies and aligned with national regulations. These services are tailored to meet the needs of the school and local community and can adapt to public health emergencies. Students are included in school councils, governance boards, and HPS design teams alongside parents, caregivers, and community members. Schools regularly evaluate their policies and resources for HPS, ensuring continuous improvement. Leadership teams collaborate with local communities to plan and monitor the progress of HPS partnerships. Teacher training and professional development opportunities are provided to support HPS leadership and implementation. Policies are in place to create a safe environment for all members of the school community, with regular checks and updates as needed. Global, national, and subnational efforts focus on monitoring and evaluating the implementation of HPS initiatives. This includes the development of indicators and metrics to assess progress and the establishment of frameworks for program evaluation. Resources and guidelines are available to support the design, planning, and implementation of HPS, addressing barriers and enablers to success. Stakeholder engagement is a critical component of HPS implementation, with tools available to identify, map, and involve stakeholders effectively. Schools are encouraged to collaborate with parents, caregivers, and local communities to promote health and well-being. Comprehensive frameworks and guidelines are provided to address school nutrition, health services, and the management of public health crises, such as the COVID-19 pandemic. In summary, the transformation of schools into health-promoting institutions involves a multi-faceted approach that integrates policy development, stakeholder collaboration, curriculum enhancement, staff training, and continuous monitoring and evaluation. These efforts aim to create a supportive environment that fosters the physical, social, and emotional well-being of students and the broader school community.
